instruction: Press the juicer's knob down until it reaches its pressed position, then let go.

outcome.real_measurement: Rationale: the released env itself defines the press target as qmin + 0.25 (qmax - qmin) = -0.218 rad for model 103105 (max_close_frac = 0.25) but never uses it; we require the knob joint to actually reach it at some point (the knob has no return spring, so min over the episode = deepest press). Real world: knob/lever angle from a joint encoder if the appliance is instrumented, otherwise an AprilTag on the knob tracked by a fixed camera (angle relative to the start frame).

Rationale: the press must be done by the robot, i.e. some robot link touches the knob link (pairwise contact force > 0.05 N, ~5 gram-force, sampled once per 20 Hz control step). Real world: fingertip tactile pads or wrist F/T spike (> 0.05 N) while the fingertip is within 1 cm of the knob in the camera / forward kinematics.

counterexamples.description: official motion-planning solution (_050); E1 showed it never moves the knob

source.released_code_predicate: success = juicer_ever_pressed = OR_t(||left TCP - knob mesh centre|| <= 0.14 m); pressed_enough (qpos <= target) computed, unused

notes: released = no robot-knob contact over the final 10 control steps (TraceRecorder 'released' signal). Contacts are taken from the last PhysX substep of each control step, so a contact shorter than 10 ms between two control steps could be missed; sustained presses are not affected.
